title: 1995 Miami Dolphins season
summary: This document covers the 1995 Miami Dolphins season, which marked the franchise's 30th season, 26th in the NFL, and notably the final season under legendary head coach Don Shula. The document begins with an overview noting the team's 9–7 record and playoff loss to the Buffalo Bills, mentioning it was the last time until 2022 that the Dolphins had a top-10 offense. The main sections of the document include the offseason activities (1995 expansion draft, NFL draft, and undrafted free agents), the team roster, and the regular season with its schedule and standings. The playoffs section details the AFC Wild Card Game, highlighting quarterback Dan Marino's performance of 33 completions on 64 attempts for 422 yards and two touchdowns, along with three interceptions, while the Bills set an NFL playoff record with 341 rushing yards. A dedicated section covers Don Shula's retirement, summarizing his NFL-record 347 career wins (257 with Miami), his six Super Bowl appearances with two victories, his leadership of the 1972 undefeated season, and his 1997 induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. The document concludes with awards and honors recognizing Dan Marino's AFC Pro Bowl and All-Pro selections, followed by notes and external references.
